label: Gift retailer, three years daily
note: Daily revenue with a clear holiday peak. December is about 163, November 146 and January 79, and the yearly trend is about +9%.

label: French month names
note: Month labels like "janv. 2022" and numbers like "1 598,00". Pick the value column by hand; the real peak is June and the low is December.

label: Day-first dates
note: The same data with dates like 01/05/2022. If it reports only a few months of data, the dates were read the wrong way round.

label: Day-first, month-end dates
note: Dates like 31/01/2022. A confident curve here may be wrong, so check that the number of years matches what you uploaded.

label: Daily, day-first dates
note: Daily moving searches with a strong May and June peak. A result that says there is no seasonality means the dates were misread.

label: Ski travel, Canada
note: Winter peak in the northern hemisphere. A clean, single-region curve.

label: Ski travel, Australia
note: Winter in Australia runs June to August, so the peak is in the middle of the year.

label: Canada and Australia combined
note: Adding two opposite seasons produces a curve that is wrong for both. Always analyze regions separately.

label: Short history with strong growth
note: 15 months of steady growth with no real seasons. The honest result is inconclusive, and the peak month it names is only the growth.

label: Travel around Lunar New Year
note: The holiday moves each year, so a fixed monthly curve misses it. The January and February split changes year to year.

label: Hourly timestamps in UTC
note: Hourly rows treated as daily show almost no weekday pattern. Total the data by day in your own time zone first.

label: Missing months and a zero month
note: Three months are missing and one month is zero because ads were paused. Fill the gaps before trusting the result.

label: Random noise, 36 months
note: There is no real pattern in this data. Any peak the tool names is chance.

label: Flat daily rate, monthly totals
note: The daily rate never changes, but monthly totals differ because months have different lengths. That is not seasonality.
